notations: K + provenance + uncertainty + authority + perspective + history + assumptions + limitations + transformations
note: S0493's refinement of an earlier chakra=knowledge-layer vertical-stack mapping into a ten-lens reference model (ontology/epistemology/cognition/perspective/DDD/cybernetics/governance/evidence/temporal/architecture/development/AI-cognition) drawn from Sankhya/consciousness sources, culminating in a 'reflexive knowledge system' formulation; explicitly a diagnostic reference model, not architecture.

S0495's first-pass extraction from Hofstadter's Godel, Escher, Bach: levels of description, conceptual skeletons as invariant structural cores, declarative/procedural/structural/meta knowledge, distributed and tangled (SHRDLU) knowledge, a strange-loop mechanism, K(K) meta-knowledge notation, and a KnowledgeState tuple with measurable dimensions; proposed as the missing bridge between the project's Zero lens and Knowledge State theory.

S0496's extraction from a 2023 Medium-article reading of the Nasadiya Sukta, compared structurally (not historically) with GEB: contributes 'knowledge includes knowledge of non-knowledge', a seven-state Knowledge State (Known/Unknown/Uncertain/Underdetermined/Unobservable/Currently-unknowable/Possibly-unknowable), an Invariant-Zero vs Boundary-Zero split, four epistemic conditions U_c/U_p/U_f/U_o, and a K=(R,M,I,P,E,B)/MetaK=K(K) formalization; explicitly flags its source as secondary/interpretive, not scholarly, and defers formalization pending a cross-source conceptual model.

aliases: Freedom Preetham 'Concept of Time in Vedas' article
note: S0497 is a verbatim externally-authored 2023 Medium article (Atharva Veda Kanda 19 Sukthas 53-54 on Time/Kaala plus a Bhagavad Gita 11.32 citation) with the external author's own block-universe and quantum-decoherence analogies; likely the raw source underlying a not-yet-processed KnowledgeOS extraction file later in this kernel sequence, by the same author as the Nasadiya Sukta article discussed in S0496 but a different sukta/article.

S0498's six-pramana (adding Arthapatti/postulation and Anupalabdhi/absence to the four-pramana Nyaya set) epistemic-acquisition model: each pramana as an operator, an epistemic vector P(C) with leave-one-pathway-out robustness, a Convergence(C) knowledge-quality metric, a refined evidence-provenance record schema, and the definition 'a proposition without epistemic lineage is a claim, not knowledge'; may be the same recurring pramana research thread as pramana-four-knowledge-sources (B0006) under a different (six-source) taxonomy, or a distinct model -- unresolved.

S0500's and S0504's extraction of catuskoti (Buddhist/Jain four-valued logic T/F/Both/Neither) as a KnowledgeOS logic layer: EpistemicState(P) in {T,F,B,N} kept strictly separate from scalar Confidence C(P), an epistemic-entropy measure, the 'both' state reinterpreted as possible scope/time/interpretation difference rather than true contradiction, an elephant-analogy projection formalization Oi=pi_i(R), and (in S0504) a tightened K(P)=(L,C,E,Q,U,D,T) knowledge vector plus a Forward(E->K)/Inverse(K->E*) evidence-sufficiency problem; recorded here as UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE in individual contributions pending resolution against zero-neutral-state-lens and other Zero variants.

aliases: Shannon/Weaver Mathematical Theory of Communication lens
note: S0506's extraction from Shannon & Weaver: Information != Meaning != Knowledge; entropy and equivocation as uncertainty measures; engineering vs semantic noise (motivating a proposed Semantic Integrity Layer); redundancy as an error-correction mechanism (duplication vs independent redundancy); channel capacity as a knowledge-delivery-capacity constraint for AI agents; Information Gain IG(E)=H(X)-H(X|E) proposed to replace similarity-based retrieval; context/Markov structure K=K(P|C,T,D); closes with two headline principles (measure uncertainty reduction, not information volume; independent redundancy is error-correction, not waste), explicitly deferred pending comparison against the frozen KnowledgeOS architecture.

S0507's four-way multi-agent review (Principal Architect / Perplexity / ChatGPT / Kimi) of the 'bounded, dynamic knowledge' conceptual model: introduces Proposition-vs-Assertion, a Conceptual Separation Matrix method, ~18 non-collapsible distinctions, ten candidate invariants (incl. 'no epistemic upgrade by transformation'), dynamic Karaka roles, tacit knowledge, scale as a dimension, and the closing methodological principle 'a lens may generate a distinction/question/test, never impose its own ontology on KnowledgeOS.'

aliases: What are we actually building when we say KnowledgeOS
note: S0509's synthesis across the S0493-S0508 lens series and DDD review: KnowledgeOS = maintains semantic/epistemic/contextual integrity of a changing body of knowledge, not a knowledge database/graph/AI-memory; Kernel = five capabilities (identity, meaning, epistemic integrity, inquiry, assessment) explicitly excluding LLMs/embeddings/ML/domain knowledge/documents/UI; four distinct boundary senses (semantic/context/epistemic/system); CHANGE as a missing dimension; a 20-row kernel/not-kernel/hypothesis classification table; closing on 'what is the smallest thing KnowledgeOS must preserve so knowledge can be expressed, questioned, challenged, evaluated, changed and reconstructed without losing identity, context, provenance or epistemic meaning?' as the real Kernel question.

S0511's application of Trenton Merricks' Objects and Persons (2001) eliminativist method to KnowledgeOS ontology discovery: a four-test admission method for candidate primitives, the 'arranged-knowledge-wise' idea (no canonical Knowledge/Knowledge-State object, only a projection over preserved structure), a structural-grounding dimension distinguishing false-but-grounded from unsupported/hallucinated claims, and a 'Non-Redundant Work Principle' -- a concept becomes a Kernel primitive only if it performs work its constituents cannot already do. Likely continues in later same-day files (S0512, S0513) given the batch's own naming pattern.

S0514/S0517's application of Colin McGinn's Logical Properties (five chapters: Identity, Existence, Predication, Necessity, Truth) as an adversarial falsification lens for a Kernel-finding exercise referencing prior 'C-n' numbered candidates (C-1, C-8, C-11) and a cross-validation table against Escher/Siva-Sakti/Zero-Wu/Vani/Triputi/Godel/Negative-Epistemology/Chinese(Yijing/Ming/Shi/Yin-Yang) lenses from an investigative thread not otherwise present in this batch's same-day sequence; contributes a systematic classification of KnowledgeOS quantification attributes into logical/epistemic/temporal/structural/social property categories, each requiring a different quantification method (binary/mode vs qualified-scalar vs state-machine vs interval vs graph).

S0515's application of Timothy O'Connor's Persons and Causes to KnowledgeOS: Cause modeled as a relation not an entity; Person distinguished from Object by agency/beliefs/desires/reasons/intentions; Capacity/Power as a bridge between what-is and what-can-do; Reason vs Cause as distinct explanation kinds; a worked KnowledgeAssertionRecord example (CAUSAL_CLAIM/EXPLANATORY_CLAIM/AGENT_CLAIM/REASON_CLAIM) showing these are preserved as content, never implemented as Kernel primitives; cross-checked against mcginn-logical-properties-lens (S0514) to distinguish Kernel-level logical properties from content-level metaphysical categories.

aliases: Information Theory as a Lens for KnowledgeOS
note: S0516's application of ten named, formal information-theory results (entropy, mutual information, channel capacity, rate-distortion, data processing inequality, source/channel coding theorems, Fano's inequality, AEP, KL divergence) as quantitative impossibility bounds for KnowledgeOS, cross-referenced against a distinct prior lens set (Zero/Wu, Yin-Yang, Vāṇī, Moksha, Escher/Śiva-Śakti, Semantic Normal Form, Ganesha threshold, Nyāya, Ziran, Navya-Nyāya, Ming) not otherwise documented in this batch; more mathematically rigorous than the earlier Shannon/Weaver conceptual treatment (shannon-weaver-information-theory-lens, S0506).

S0520's research-planning document setting a reading order (Floridi, Williamson, Dretske, Fagin/Halpern/Moses/Vardi, Brachman/Levesque, Brandom, Searle) for defining the Knowledge Space Kernel, each with a Zero Lens question; proposes a 19-question per-book 'Zero-Lens Extraction' protocol feeding a cross-book-intersection pipeline, and a central hypothesis that Knowledge Space has three primitive dimensions (Ontological, Semantic, Epistemic) unified by Modal/Temporal structure with Truth bridging Ontological and Semantic. This batch's own subsequent files (Floridi S0521, Dretske S0522, Fagin/Halpern/Moses/Vardi S0523) execute this roadmap.

S0521's extraction from Floridi's Philosophy of Information: Levels of Abstraction as a non-ontological, purpose/scope-relative account of Knowledge-Space boundaries; the semantic-information chain (data->well-formed->meaningful->truthful->relevant->accounted->knowledge); the Network Theory of Account (Question->Answer->Account cycle, why-questions split into causal/functional/historical/teleological); a family-of-spaces hypothesis (Data/Semantic/Epistemic/State/Modal/Inference spaces related via LoA); named 'Knowledge Space Model v0.2', explicitly not yet frozen pending further lenses (Williamson next per the S0520 roadmap).

aliases: Dretske Knowledge and the Flow of Information lens
note: S0522's extraction from Dretske: information ≠ meaning (Event/State->Information->Coding->Meaning->Belief->Knowledge); information as reduction of a possibility space; a channel/calibration distinction between knowledge-about-domain, knowledge-about-evidence-source, and knowledge-about-observation-mechanism-reliability; information-caused belief as an alternative to Floridi's relevance+account route to knowledge; nested informational shells reframing 'knowledge depth'; Information ≠ Belief ≠ Knowledge; and a representation-independence principle. Read explicitly in comparison with floridi-philosophy-of-information-lens (S0521), proposing a Floridi x Dretske comparative matrix as the next step.

S0523's extraction from Fagin/Halpern/Moses/Vardi's Reasoning About Knowledge: the possible-worlds Kripke structure, the principle that no single model of knowledge is uniquely correct, the common-knowledge hierarchy (individual/E(P)/E^2(P)/C(P), muddy-children example), ascribed/external vs algorithmic/computable knowledge, distributed knowledge, non-monotonic knowledge over time, and a final formal Knowledge Space tuple K=(S,P,π,A,~,T,E,C) with K_a(P,s). The first of the four-book McGinn/Floridi/Dretske/Fagin thread to reach a genuinely formalizable core; explicitly still not frozen as the Kernel.

S0528's extraction from Peter Gärdenfors' Knowledge in Flux: epistemic states (not knowledge) as the primary modeling unit; expansion/revision/contraction as the three fundamental change types; epistemic entrenchment as a contextual, regime-dependent resistance-to-revision dimension distinct from probability; propositions modeled as state transformations P:K->K'; explanation as surprise-reduction relative to the recipient's epistemic state; causal belief modeled via contraction; a three-level preserved-history/epistemic-state/presented-knowledge architecture. Ranked by the author as one of the most useful sources read in the whole McGinn-Floridi-Dretske-Fagin-Gärdenfors research arc.

notations: X counts as Y in C
aliases: Searle Construction of Social Reality lens
note: S0534's extraction from Searle's The Construction of Social Reality: brute vs institutional facts via the X-counts-as-Y-in-C formula, refined to Status(X,Y,C)/StatusFunction(X,Y,C); deontic power distinct from causal power; collective intentionality; institutional facts as relational networks depending on brute facts; primacy of process over object (Marriage/Government/Election/Corporation/Money/Contract/Office as maintained practices); expressive vs constitutive language and descriptive assertion vs constitutive/performative act; Searle's 'background' capacities as a further reason not all knowledge is linguistically explicit; a ten-item Zero-Lens residual list (ZL-S01..ZL-S10); and a proposed Institutional Space branch of the Knowledge Space diagram alongside Natural and Semantic space. Sixth book in the McGinn/Floridi/Dretske/Fagin/Gärdenfors/Searle research arc.
